article.headline: What should a generated world remember?
article.lead: L3G-World keeps a compact 3D Gaussian representation of a scene as the viewpoint moves. Revisiting a location makes the value of that memory tangible: objects placed earlier should still occupy the same space.

picks.question: How does consistency on a return visit change as the memory uses fewer 3D primitives?

paragraphs.text: L3G-World stores scene information in latent 3D Gaussians. A camera can leave a region and later revisit its representation. The paper's long-horizon experiments are a better place to assess that design than a short fly-through.

HairDeck and SpecSlot operate at smaller scales. HairDeck treats each stylized hair card as a token, producing animation-ready cards from a single image. SpecSlot assigns distinct frequency components to slots so that preserving fine image detail need not require a longer global attention sequence.

sections.heading: Choosing a model before starting a media job

paragraphs.text: The scenario-labs/skills repository packages image, video, audio and 3D generation workflows for agents. It puts model choice and cost estimates before execution, a practical feature when the same creative request can be sent to several media services.
